text:
Marta: customer filed ticket saying EventSource stream goes blank after a 304 from their CDN in Safari 16. They use htmx to swap fragments and keep an SSE connection open. Repro steps attached by customer.

Devon: ack, can you paste the network headers and a short repro? Does the browser show the connection as closed or still open but no events? :eyes:

Marta: paste from customer: 

---- network dump ----
GET /sse/stream HTTP/1.1
Host: cdn.example.net
Accept: text/event-stream
Cookie: session=abc123; SameSite=None; Secure
Origin: https://app.customer.com

200 -> 304 (from cache)
Response headers on 304: 
HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified
Cache-Control: max-age=3600
Date: Tue, 10 May 2026 14:12:22 GMT
Vary: Accept-Encoding

Customer says after that the EventSource stops receiving messages (blank) and polyfill doesn't attempt reconnect.

Samir: htmx plus Safari is a weird combo. Two quick things: 1) Safari historically treats 304 and cached responses oddly for EventSource, especially if Transfer-Encoding/Content-Length isn't passed through. 2) CDN might be serving 304 with Cache-Control that indicates it can satisfy the request from cache, but EventSource expects a streaming response with chunked encoding.

Alex: can we get them to try bypassing CDN to confirm? e.g., curl -v with --raw to see if server sends `Content-Type: text/event-stream` and `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` on the origin stream.

Marta: customer ran origin vs CDN: origin keeps sending chunked data, works fine. Through CDN they get 304 and the connection closes for Safari. Chrome keeps reconnecting.

Devon: okay that nails down a CDN caching quirk. Two mitigation paths: (A) change CDN rules so SSE endpoints bypass cache or use Cache-Control: no-store/no-cache; must-revalidate; or set surrogate-control: no-store; or (B) add cache-busting param to the SSE URL for Safari users. Also ensure the CDN doesn't respond 304 for streaming endpoints.

Samir: also check response headers on the streaming path when the CDN is the origin agent for the client. If the CDN converts a streaming response into a cached 304 then EventSource in Safari might treat that as a completed response and not fire the open/reconnect logic. Safari-specific note: older Safari won't reopen EventSource after a 304 if it thinks the resource was served from cache. :thinking:

Alex: can we confirm the CDN preserves `Connection: keep-alive` and `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`? If the CDN strips chunked or collapses to a 304, EventSource won't have the event framing. Ask customer to share full response headers including `x-cache` headers.

Marta: they sent this extra dump: 

--- via CDN ---
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Cache-Control: max-age=3600
X-Cache: HIT
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Content-Type: text/event-stream

...streaming... then later server replies 304 for a conditional request from their browser. After that browser shows "(re)open" in devtools but no events.

Devon: hmm, two observations: 1) 304 for SSE is atypical — many CDNs will either always return 200 and stream or treat SSE as non-cacheable. 2) If conditional requests are enabled between browser and CDN (If-Modified-Since / If-None-Match), Safari may rely on cached payload and not re-establish the streaming parser.

Marta: quick repro snippet they used: 

```js
// client
const es = new EventSource('/sse/stream');
es.onmessage = e => console.log('evt', e.data);
es.onerror = e => console.log('es error', e);
```

Customer also uses an htmx snippet that swaps fragments while SSE runs. Noticed the blankness happens after navigation or fragment swap triggers conditional requests.

Samir: recommend instructing CDN to: 
- mark SSE endpoints as Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate OR set `Surrogate-Control: no-store` for edge caches
- disable conditional GET/If-Modified-Since for that path so CDN returns 200 streaming rather than 304
- preserve Transfer-Encoding and do not convert streaming responses to cached 304s

Alex: we should also tell customers to ensure cookies/authorization aren't being stripped by the CDN on conditional requests. If the CDN responds from cache without revalidating the Authorization or Cookie, Safari may get confused. Also Vary headers: ensure `Vary: Cookie` or `Vary: Authorization` if relevant.

Marta: customer asked if polyfill can help. They use an EventSource polyfill that triggers XHR fallback. Polyfill logs show the fallback never runs after 304 because the polyfill sees the stream as finished.

Devon: fallback won't help if browser never gets an error event. So server/CDN side is primary fix. But we can suggest client workaround: monitor readyState and force a reconnect when you detect long silence. e.g., setTimeout to ping server and if no events in N seconds close() then new EventSource(). Not ideal but a stopgap.

Alex: propose triage steps for support response: 
1) Ask them to temporarily bypass CDN (already done, origin OK).
2) Have CDN set `Cache-Control: no-store` for SSE path and disable conditional GETs.
3) Ensure edge returns `200` and preserves `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and Content-Type.
4) If CDN can't be configured, add cache-buster query for SSE for Safari user-agent.
5) Provide minimal client-side watchdog snippet as fallback.

Samir: adding exact header examples to pass to CDN ops: 

```
Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store, must-revalidate, max-age=0
Surrogate-Control: no-store
Vary: User-Agent, Accept-Encoding
Content-Type: text/event-stream
Connection: keep-alive
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
```

Also recommend removing `ETag`/`Last-Modified` for that route so conditional 304s aren't issued.

Marta: i'll send that to the customer and ask them to request their CDN vendor to treat SSE as non-cacheable. I'll include the watchdog snippet.

Alex: add note for internal: we should document common CDN behaviors with SSE and maintain a KB article. I'll open a doc and ping infra team to add a rule template for customers.

deploy-bot: deployment queued: sse-edge-helpers-docs -> draft created (#PR-2345) :white_check_mark:

Marta: thanks all. I'll reply to ticket with the CDN header suggestions, troubleshooting steps, and a temporary client watchdog. Will follow up after customer confirms. :thumbsup:
